note: Conference paragraphs as the study API publishes them. Do not hand-edit "text": run `python tools/test_quotes.py --refresh`. A paragraph's id is the `id=` in the link a card builds.

cases.reference: Neil L. Andersen, "Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey" (April 2026), p_ozqOI
cases.why: 'that day' is the day the paragraph before it describes -- kneeling across the altar from Kathy in a holy temple of God. Alone on a card it asks the reader to remember a day it never names. The paragraph reported as broken.
cases.text: To you in this vast worldwide congregation who lovingly remember that day in your life, I speak especially to you.

cases.reference: Neil L. Andersen, "Eternal Marriage Is an Eternal Journey" (April 2026), p_nioDZ
cases.why: The same fault one paragraph further on. 'At that moment, kneeling across the altar' points back at the same day, and the talk had both paragraphs in the calendar.
cases.text: At that moment, kneeling across the altar, we have a growing realization of the depth of our commitment to God and to each other. The sacred ordinance binds us together with our eternal companion and with God. We solemnly vow to keep the covenants, and the Lord promises us, as we are faithful, unspeakable blessings in mortality and beyond, including thrones, powers, and dominions in the eternal world.

cases.reference: Taniela B. Wakolo, "Come unto Christ--Together" (April 2026), p_uyAJC
cases.why: 'These stories are not about statistics.' A story cannot be the one the speaker is standing in, so 'these' points backwards exactly as 'those' would. Read cold, there are no stories.
cases.text: Brothers and sisters, God keeps His promises—but in His timing. These stories are not about statistics. They are about souls.

cases.reference: Emily Belle Freeman, "Best Days and Worst Days" (April 2026), p_fiYks
cases.why: 'How do we get through those days?' -- a plural points out of its paragraph as readily as a singular, and which days is the whole question.
cases.text: How do we get through those days? The story of Peter teaches us that strength comes as we walk with Christ and hold fast to His eternal truths.

cases.reference: Henry B. Eyring, "All Will Be Well Because of Temple Covenants" (April 2024), p8
cases.why: An earlier conference, so the rule is not read as being about one talk. 'At that moment' is the moment he told his wife that all would be well because of the temple, and that is in the paragraph before.
cases.text: At that moment, it was as if the Spirit of the Lord confirmed in our hearts and minds what we both already knew to be true: the sealing ordinances, found only in the house of the Lord and administered by proper priesthood authority, had bound us together as husband and wife, and our children had been sealed to us. There truly was no need to fear, and we were grateful later to learn that our boys were safe.

cases.reference: Amy A. Wright, "Abide the Day in Christ" (October 2023), p20
cases.why: 'In that moment every family home evening lesson ... mattered.' The moment is the peace that came over her in the paragraph before, and this one never says so.
cases.text: In that moment every family home evening lesson, scripture study session, prayer of faith offered, blessing given, testimony shared, covenant made and kept, house of the Lord attended, and Sabbath day observed mattered—oh, how it mattered! It was too late to put oil in our lamps. We needed every single drop, and we needed it right now!

cases.reference: Russell M. Nelson, "The Lord Jesus Christ Will Come Again" (October 2024), p_zKh76
cases.why: 'That day will be filled with joy for the righteous.' An occasion still ahead is not one a speaker has already narrated, and the day of the Lord is a day every reader can name.
cases.text: I bear my solemn witness that Jesus Christ is the Son of God. I am His disciple. I am honored to be His servant. At His Second Coming, “the glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together.” That day will be filled with joy for the righteous!

cases.reference: Neil L. Andersen, "The Atoning Love of Jesus Christ" (October 2025), p_coIZa
cases.why: 'That moment will come. I testify that it will come.' The same exemption, and the paragraph has already described the moment in its own words.
cases.text: As you continue to place your trust in Him, your clouds of darkness and anguished sobbing in the night will be transformed into cascading tears of joy and peace in the morning’s light. “Your sorrow shall be turned into joy. … And your joy no [one] taketh from you.” That moment will come. I testify that it will come.

cases.reference: Eduardo F. Ortega, "Christ--Author and Finisher of Our Faith" (April 2026), p_ypdOG
cases.why: 'The perspective that time gives' is a relative clause, not a pointer: the 'that' is the object of 'gives' and 'time' is its subject. The one paragraph in the whole conference cache where the exemption is needed, and the reason it takes two signals rather than one.
cases.text: In addition to the changes you may have already experienced in your lives and hearts, there is a road ahead for you to “press forward with a steadfastness in Christ” as you endure on the covenant path. In doing so, perhaps you will experience the same as I have; sometimes I need the perspective that time gives to see the refining and perfecting hand of our Savior, Jesus Christ, in my life and in my family’s life.

cases.reference: Steven J. Lund, "Divine Authority, Sublime Young Men" (April 2025), p_vqEMC
cases.why: Its 'that morning' is filled -- the paragraph opened on 'The next morning', so it has already said which, and `unnamed_occasion` keeps it. It goes out all the same, because 'The next morning' opens the next scene of a story: whose little girl, and why the bishop's family might stay home, are in the paragraphs before. Uchtdorf below now holds the exemption this case used to.
cases.text: The next morning their ward members gathered for sacrament meeting filled with compassion, also suffering over the loss of this perfect little girl. No one expected the bishop’s family to be at church that morning, but a couple of minutes before the meeting started, they quietly entered and took their place.

cases.reference: Dieter F. Uchtdorf, "Encounter at the Empty Tomb" (April 2026), p_zly6F
cases.why: 'Because of those experiences' -- named a sentence earlier in the same paragraph, 'sacred spiritual experiences and knowledge', so the 'those' has its answer at hand. The exemption for an occasion the paragraph names itself, on a paragraph that is otherwise a quote.
cases.text: The Savior has entrusted each of us personally with sacred spiritual experiences and knowledge. Because of those experiences, we can see for ourselves the meaning of the empty tomb: that Jesus Christ lives and is actively blessing all who seek Him.

cases.reference: Gregorio E. Casillas, "God Loves All His Children" (October 2024), p_m8wzU
cases.why: 'on that day when a priesthood leader felt impressed for us to visit a mother and a son' -- the clause after it says which day.
cases.text: My dear brothers and sisters, on that day when a priesthood leader felt impressed for us to visit a mother and a son that we did not have on our agenda, I proclaim that God knew they needed us. And at the end, I was the one who was ministered to. On that day, I received one of the greatest lessons of the Savior’s love for us.

cases.reference: Ruben V. Alliaud, "Sons and Daughters of God" (October 2024), p_daJuY
cases.why: 'that moment of weakness' -- an 'of' complement says which moment as plainly as a clause does.
cases.text: In this context, Satan’s request to worship him may have been only a distraction. A significant temptation for Moses in that moment of weakness was to become confused and believe that he was only a “son of man,” rather than a child of God.

cases.reference: Russell M. Nelson, "The Lord Jesus Christ Will Come Again" (October 2024), p_leSJJ
cases.why: 'I pray that we will not miss the majesty of this moment!' 'This moment' is the one the speaker is standing in and wants nothing from any paragraph. Pinned so the rule is not later widened from 'that' to 'this' for the words that can mean now.
cases.text: My dear brothers and sisters, do you see what is happening right before our eyes? I pray that we will not miss the majesty of this moment! The Lord is indeed hastening His work.

cases.reference: Neil L. Andersen, "Temples, Houses of the Lord Dotting the Earth" (April 2024), p25
cases.why: 'In this day of confusion and commotion' -- the same deictic 'this', in the other word the rule leaves alone.
cases.text: In this day of confusion and commotion, I testify that the temple is His holy house and will help preserve us, protect us, and prepare us for the glorious day when, with all His holy angels, our Savior returns in majesty, power, and great glory. In the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

cases.reference: Ulisses Soares, "A Higher and Holier Fast" (October 2026), p_a8hXF
cases.why: Ends on a curly closing quotation mark, as every paragraph that closes on someone's words does. Asking for the straight one instead refused a fifth of the conference whatever it said, this whole talk among it.

Smith taught that proper fasting “would … place the body in subjection to the spirit, and so promote communion with the Holy Ghost” and that “this law would bring [us] nearer to God.”

cases.reference: Neil L. Andersen, "Cherishing Life" (April 2025), p_wnNG2
cases.why: Ends on a closing quotation mark too, but opens inside the quotation: the tail of a statement begun in the paragraph before. Accepting the curly mark must not let half a quotation through.

cases.reference: Clark G. Gilbert, "Teach Truth with Love" (October 2026), p_ivQn2
cases.why: 'The third principle is to be a light.' Read cold, the card promises a list it never shows -- the counting-off ENUMERATION refuses, in the form that names the item.
cases.text: The third principle is to be a light. President Nelson taught: “Let your skeptical friends see how much you love the Lord and His gospel. Surprise their doubting hearts with your believing heart!” The best way to help someone else keep their covenants is to keep your covenants. As Sister Tamara Runia reminded us, “Stay at the tree, … continue to beckon to those you love … that eating the fruit is a happy thing!”

cases.reference: Clark G. Gilbert, "Teach Truth with Love" (October 2026), p_hcywb
cases.why: 'Now, the fourth principle is to hold to truth' -- the same, with the turn of the talk in front of it.
cases.text: Now, the fourth principle is to hold to truth even in our outreach. In April, President Oaks stated that showing love for others “does not mean surrendering our values. The covenants we have made inevitably position us as devoted participants in the eternal contest between truth and error.”

cases.reference: Gerrit W. Gong, "'Tis Eastertide: No One Walks Alone" (April 2026), p_eUdK0
cases.why: 'The Second Comforter Jesus speaks of is Himself.' An ordinal with a capital is part of a name, and the paragraph is about that, not about a list. Pinned so the rule never goes case-blind.
cases.text: The Second Comforter Jesus speaks of is Himself. Jesus promises, “I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.”

cases.reference: Edward Dube, "Come unto Christ" (October 2026), p_ocN6I
cases.why: 'Thirty-nine years ago, President Dallin H. Oaks taught me about the character of Jesus Christ in a way I will never forget.' The first line of a story, and what he taught is in the paragraphs after it.
cases.text: Thirty-nine years ago, President Dallin H. Oaks taught me about the character of Jesus Christ in a way I will never forget.

cases.reference: Dale G. Renlund, "How Long Will It Be Ere They Believe Me?" (October 2026), p_r8684
cases.why: 'In the late 1980s, Mr. Martin developed severe heart failure.' A decade sets a scene; the lesson Mr. Martin's heart teaches is told later.
cases.text: In the late 1980s, Mr. Martin developed severe heart failure. Despite the most advanced medications available, his heart could not adequately support his circulation. He would die without a heart transplant. He became my team’s patient, and the wait for a donor heart began. His condition worsened, and mechanical pumps were implanted to sustain his life.

cases.reference: Patricio M. Giuffra, "Trusting the Lord Through Tithes and Offerings" (October 2026), p_lZ7z9
cases.why: 'The next morning, I called my mission president' -- the middle of a story, with the 'someone in her circumstances' it is about back in the paragraph before.
cases.text: The next morning, I called my mission president, President Fernando Caballero, to seek his counsel. In my mind, I wondered whether the Lord might have an exception for someone in her circumstances.

cases.reference: Michael John U. Teh, "Follow the Prophet; He Knows the Way" (April 2026), p_u8Dun
cases.why: 'In October 2024, President Dallin H. Oaks gave the following counsel' dates a teaching rather than starting a story, and the counsel follows in full. A year alone is why it is kept, where a decade or a time ago is refused.
cases.text: In October 2024, President Dallin H. Oaks gave the following counsel: “Following Christ is not a casual or occasional practice. It is a continuous commitment and way of life that should guide us at all times and in all places. His teachings and His example define the path for every disciple of Jesus Christ. And all are invited to this path.”

cases.reference: Dallin H. Oaks, "Closing Remarks" (October 2026), p_gxEuv
cases.why: 'Following this session of general conference, the first episode of a dynamic video series, Dedicate, will premiere' -- an announcement, read on some other day entirely. It scored as a promise because of 'More will come'.
cases.text: Following this session of general conference, the first episode of a dynamic video series, Dedicate, will premiere worldwide in multiple languages. More will come in the months ahead, including a virtual tour of the Salt Lake Temple.

cases.reference: Vaiangina Sikahema, "Prophets, Seers, and Revelators" (October 2026), p_hWszk
cases.why: 'As we begin this opening session of the 196th Semiannual General Conference' -- a session is only ever 'this' one from the pulpit.
cases.text: What a blessing it is to live in a time when apostles and prophets are on the earth. As we begin this opening session of the 196th Semiannual General Conference of the Church, let us not be guilty of holding “the oracles of God … as a light thing” (Doctrine and Covenants 90:5).

cases.reference: Ronald A. Rasband, "Behold I Am the Light Which Ye Shall Hold Up" (October 2024), p_z6Ad2
cases.why: 'To the many testimonies at this conference, I add my apostolic witness that Jesus Christ is the Son of God' -- 'this conference' is often the frame for a witness that stands on its own. Pinned so the session rule is not widened to the conference.
cases.text: To the many testimonies at this conference, I add my apostolic witness that Jesus Christ is the Son of God, our Lord and Savior, the Redeemer of all of our Father’s children. By His Atonement, Jesus Christ made it possible for us, if we are worthy, to return to the presence of our Father in Heaven and be with our families for eternity.

cases.reference: D. Todd Christofferson, "O Be Wise" (October 2026), p_sQ6YV
cases.why: 'The Apostle Paul noted in his day ... But he cautioned the disciples to abstain anyway.' What held then, and nothing of why, or of what it asks now -- set up and never paid off.
cases.text: The Apostle Paul noted in his day that someone with a firm belief in Christ could eat food sacrificed to idols without intending it as a sign of idol worship; it would just be a meal. But he cautioned the disciples to abstain anyway.

cases.reference: Quentin L. Cook, "Integrity and Virtue Lead to Happiness" (October 2026), p_jN1eQ
cases.why: 'In our day, the application of this principle is essential' -- our day is the reader's, so this is the teaching brought home rather than left in the past.
cases.text: In our day, the application of this principle is essential if we are to be true lifelong disciples of Christ. We need to live our lives with integrity and follow His example. The Lord, speaking of one servant in Nauvoo, declared, “He may be trusted because of the integrity of his heart.” Preach My Gospel teaches, “Integrity includes being honest with God, yourself, your leaders, and others.”

cases.reference: Michael A. Dunn, "The Ninety and Ten" (October 2026), p_ov9vM
cases.why: 'In a gentle, reassuring tone, he reminded me of the months of preparation' -- a scene, with a 'he' the paragraph never names.
cases.text: In a gentle, reassuring tone, he reminded me of the months of preparation and those early-morning runs. He then kneeled down, looked me in the eye, and said something I will never forget: “I know you can do this, Mike, and I’m going to get you there.”

cases.reference: Clark G. Gilbert, "Teach Truth with Love" (October 2026), p_jco7G
cases.why: 'President Jeffrey R. Holland similarly reminded us' -- a named speaker's reminder is a quotation, not a scene. Only the pronoun storyteller is refused.
cases.text: President Jeffrey R. Holland similarly reminded us, “Jesus clearly understood what many in our modern culture seem to forget: that there is a crucial difference between the commandment to forgive sin (which He had an infinite capacity to do) and the warning against condoning it (which He never ever did even once).”

cases.reference: Patricio M. Giuffra, "Trusting the Lord Through Tithes and Offerings" (October 2026), p_b19YT

cases.reference: Edward Dube, "Come unto Christ" (October 2026), p_x2pcP

cases.text: To him, and to all who feel that same ache, I invite you, please come unto Christ and embrace His promise, “that [His] joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full.”
